How to Install Ubuntu 26.04 LTS – Complete Beginner's Guide
What immutable Linux distros are and whether you should use one
recent_posts.summary: Immutable Linux distributions ship the entire OS as a single versioned, read-only image instead of individual packages. This design improves stability, resists tampering, and enables reliable rollbacks — without removing the ability to customize. User data, configs, and applications persist normally; only the base OS layer is locked. Different distros implement immutability differently: Fedora Atomic uses OSTree, openSUSE MicroOS uses transactional updates with Btrfs snapshots, and Ubuntu Core uses an A/B partition model. Applications are typically managed via Flatpak or package layering outside the base OS. While immutable distros are still maturing and not yet the default for most use cases, they are gaining real-world adoption (e.g., SteamOS on Steam Deck) and represent a meaningful architectural shift in how Linux systems are managed.

recent_posts.title: lnav Tutorial: Analyze Linux Log Files Like a Pro
recent_posts.summary: A practical introduction to lnav (Log File Navigator), a terminal utility for analyzing Linux log files. Covers installation across major distros, basic navigation with colorized output, jumping between errors and warnings, merging multiple log files into a unified timeline, searching, filtering with filter-in and filter-out commands, and tailing live logs with the -t flag. Also demonstrates the histogram and timeline views for visualizing log activity over time.

recent_posts.title: Are IT Certifications Worth It in 2026?
recent_posts.summary: A practical look at the real value of IT certifications for system administrators and aspiring IT professionals. Certifications can help with career growth, but their impact on hiring depends heavily on the individual employer. The primary value lies in structured skill development and accountability rather than guaranteed job offers. The post covers vendor-neutral vs. vendor-specific certifications, overviews LPI, CompTIA, Linux Foundation, and Red Hat options, and advises focusing on a small, targeted set of certifications rather than collecting as many as possible. Expensive boot camps are discouraged in favor of self-study.

recent_posts.title: Manage, Backup, and Restore Flatpak Apps with Warehouse
recent_posts.summary: Warehouse is a GUI utility for managing Flatpak applications on Linux. It lets you view installed Flatpaks, inspect and delete user data, manage repositories (remotes), take snapshots of app state for backup/restore, and install new Flatpaks directly. The video also covers setting up Flatpak and Flathub from scratch on Debian with GNOME, including installing the GNOME Software plugin and adding the Flathub repository.

recent_posts.title: System76 Thelio Mira 2026 review for Linux desktop users
recent_posts.summary: A full review of the 2026 System76 Thelio Mira Linux desktop. The redesigned chassis features a milled metal front IO bar, tempered glass panel, aluminum and steel construction, and a new liquid cooling system that improves performance by up to 19% and reduces temperatures by 13°. The review unit scored over 3500 single-core and 2100 multi-core on Geekbench 6, handled Cyberpunk 2077 without stuttering, and stayed quiet under load. Pop OS 24.04 with the new Cosmic desktop environment comes pre-installed and works flawlessly out of the box. Fedora also ran well with minor Nvidia driver setup, while Debian 13 had compatibility issues due to the bleeding-edge hardware. The main criticism is the absence of a built-in card reader. Pricing starts at $1,699 for the base configuration.

recent_posts.title: System76 Launch Keyboard review for Linux users
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on review of the refreshed System76 Launch Keyboard, a premium mechanical keyboard starting at $285. Key highlights include a milled aluminum chassis, double-shot PBT keycaps, a built-in 4-port USB 3.2 hub, fully open-source hardware and firmware, and a cross-platform configurator supporting Linux, macOS, and Windows equally. The configurator allows key remapping, RGB customization, and multi-layer layouts, with all settings stored on the keyboard itself. The reviewer praises the build quality, typing comfort, and Linux-first philosophy, but notes the limited tilt adjustment as a minor downside. Existing Launch Keyboard owners are advised the upgrade is not urgent, while new buyers are recommended to consider it if budget allows.

top_posts.title: My Linux Daily Driver: A Complete Setup Overview
top_posts.summary: The author discusses their current daily driver Linux distribution, revealing a switch from Pop!_OS to Fedora with the Cosmic Desktop environment. They highlight the features and customization options of their setup, including their use of workspaces and tiling. The post also covers the choice of web browsers (Vivaldi and Microsoft Edge), the use of the Homarr custom start page, and several applications such as Audacious for music playback and Genie for text editing. The post aims to inform and inspire users about configuring their own Linux setup.

top_posts.title: Ubuntu 25.04 review: stability and refinement
top_posts.summary: Ubuntu 25.04 offers significant improvements with Linux kernel 6.14 and GNOME 48. The release includes performance enhancements like triple buffering and HDR support for displays. While some new features may have limited impact, it is praised for its stability and refined details. The upgraded installer adds new capabilities aimed at system admins. Despite these advancements, the reviewer prefers Fedora for its pure GNOME experience but acknowledges Ubuntu’s quality and recommends the latest version.

top_posts.title: Switching to Linux? Here's the Pros and Cons
top_posts.summary: Switching to Linux offers both pros and cons. Benefits include being free from licensing restrictions, high customization options, and an excellent platform for developers. On the downside, users may face limited software and hardware compatibility, fewer available games for gamers, and potential challenges with the Linux community. Despite this, the flexibility and learning opportunities provided by Linux can make it a rewarding experience.

top_posts.title: Netdata Complete Tutorial – A Full Course on Server Monitoring (Episode 4)
top_posts.summary: This tutorial explores the use of Netdata for monitoring server metrics, focusing on both core and application-specific data. The unique feature of Netdata is its ability to monitor metrics in real-time per second intervals, providing high granularity. The tutorial highlights how Netdata automatically profiles servers, displaying relevant metrics based on the applications installed. It also discusses Netdata's dynamic adjustment capabilities using collectors and its compatibility with StatsD and Openmetrics, allowing for extensive customization and integration with tailored applications.
